This is the course website and source repository for MATH 5200: Computing Using R & Python.

The course provides a fast-paced introduction to **Python and R** for graduate study in mathematics and statistics. In addition to programming fundamentals, we will study computational thinking, numerical computing, data management, testing and debugging, version control, reproducibility, and other practices used in professional computational work.

::: {.callout-important}
## Start Here

If you are new to the course, begin with **[Getting Started](getting-started.qmd)**.

It contains instructions for:

- installing the required software;
- setting up Python and the course virtual environment;
- configuring VS Code;
- obtaining and updating the course repository; and
- running the course's Quarto examples.
:::

## Course Materials

### Lectures

Lecture materials are organized by week. Each lecture generally has two components:

- **Class materials** contain exercises and examples that we will work through together in class.
- **Lecture notes** provide additional background and explanation.

[View the lecture materials](lectures.qmd)

### Homework

Homework assignments are designed to give you practice applying the ideas introduced in class.

[View the homework assignments](homework/)

### Quizzes

Short quizzes will be used to reinforce important concepts and provide regular feedback on your progress.

[View the quizzes](quizzes/)

### Semester Project

The semester project is an extended computational project in which you will apply the tools and ideas from the course to a problem of your choosing.

[Project description and instructions](project/)

## Software and Tools

The course uses:

- **Python 3**
- **R**
- **Visual Studio Code**
- **Quarto**
- **Git**
- **GitHub**

You do not need to be an expert with any of these tools at the beginning of the course. We will learn the relevant parts as we go.

The course repository itself is part of the course. You will use Git and GitHub to obtain course materials and will learn how version control fits into a reproducible computational workflow.

## Repository

The complete source for the course materials is available on GitHub:

**[Course GitHub Repository](https://github.com/moninp/intro-programming)**

The repository contains both the source files used to create this website and the programming materials used in the course.

You are encouraged to look at the source files as well as the rendered materials. In particular, the `.qmd` files that produce the lecture pages are themselves part of the course materials.

## Getting Help

If you encounter a problem with the software or course materials, please consult **[Getting Started](getting-started.qmd)**.

If you still cannot resolve the problem, please contact the instructor or bring the problem to class or office hours.

When asking for help with programming, it is particularly useful to provide:

1. the code you ran;
2. the error message or unexpected result;
3. what you expected to happen; and
4. what you have already tried.

Learning to describe a computational problem clearly is itself an important programming skill.
